newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - APRIL 28.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - APRIL 28.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- Representatives of employees demand an average wage increase of about 20 percent for 1998, more than the government and employers proposed.
- The Peruvian police detained a 30-year old Hungarian man, at whom more than nine kilograms of cocaine was found.
- Participants of a conference in Budapest said that the expectations of Hungarians from the potential Europen Union membership of the country are exaggerated.
- Peter Liszkay, who left his post as chief legal adviser at the state privatisation agency APV in a scandal over irregular payments last year, won a lawsuit against APV.
